newsitem.title: INDIA: India's RBI introduces general refinance norms.
newsitem.headline: India's RBI introduces general refinance norms.

text.p: The Reserve Bank of India on Tuesday in its credit policy for the first half of 1997/98 (April-March) introduced general refinance norms for banks.

"..with a view to enabling bank rate to emerge as a reference rate, a new refinance facility is being introduced, which would enable banks to tide over their temporary liquidity shortages," the RBI said in a statement.
Beginning the fortnight April 26, 1997, banks will be provided general refinance of 1.0 percent of their respective fortnightly average outstanding aggregate deposits in 1996/97.

The refinance facility would be two durations of four weeks each. Interest on the first four weeks will be the bank rate, the second four week stretch would attract an additional one percentage point, the RBI said.
The central bank cut the bank rate to 11 percent from the current 12 percent effective the close of business on April 15.
The entitlement under this facility to the banking system will be 46 billion rupees, it added.
